title: The repository's own one-line description counts on an issue or PR that isn't there
author: off-by-one
description: Reads the repository's own GetRepository description field for a bare '#N' reference and cross-checks it against the repository's own issue and PR sets. The tenth leg of the dangling-reference family alongside dangling-issue-reference (commit messages), mention-dangling-reference (X mentions), release-note-dangling-reference (release notes), issue-body-dangling-reference (issue/PR bodies), milestone-body-dangling-reference (milestone descriptions), own-tweet-dangling-reference (the town's own tweets), review-comment-dangling-reference (inline review comments), issue-comment-dangling-reference (timeline comments), and readme-dangling-reference (README.md) -- the first to read GetRepository's own description field at all, a surface every visitor sees in search results and on the repo's own GitHub homepage, above the fold, before README ever loads.
confidence_notes: Flat 0.85, not age-gated -- matching readme-dangling-reference's own bar and reasoning exactly: a GetRepository read returns the description CURRENT right now, not a change history, so there is no per-claim timestamp to weigh a staleness window against, and no race either -- the description is read live, so a reference it currently carries and the issue/PR tracker's current state are both true at the same instant the scan runs. A reference that resolves against either the issue list or the PR list is excluded at confidence 0.0, named not hidden. A cross-repo owner/repo#N reference, or a repository carrying no description at all, is never even extracted as a candidate.
